This ancient settlement, born from the ashes of the Lý Dynasty, when the imperial court relocated to Thăng Long, has been a hub of ceramic craftsmanship for centuries.

The unique identifying feature is the intertwined spiral cone blocks with gaps soaring straight up to the sky, majestically standing by the tranquil canal, adjacent to the main road bustling with vehicles full of ceramics passing by. As we wander through the village, the air is filled with the sweet scent of clay and the soft glow of kilns, as artisans tirelessly work day and night by their pottery wheels, their hands moving in perfect harmony with the earth and fire.
